sections.body: People around the world have different beliefs. Some follow a religion, some don't.
Some of the biggest religions are Christianity, Islam, Hinduism and Buddhism. There are many others, like Sikhism and Judaism.
Each has special places (churches, mosques, temples, gurdwaras, synagogues), special books and festivals.
Many people aren't religious and find meaning in other ways. Everyone deserves respect.
This lesson describes beliefs; it doesn't tell children what to believe. Share your family's own views alongside it.

quiz.q: Where do Muslims often go to pray together?
hints: The lesson lists special places for each religion.
Christians often pray in a church. Muslims often pray in a…?
quiz.explain: Many Muslims pray together in a mosque.

quiz.q: Your friend has a different belief from you. What's the kind thing to do?
hints: How would you want to be treated?
Different beliefs can still be friends.
If your friend likes a different football team, you can still be friends. Beliefs are similar.
quiz.explain: Respecting each other's beliefs is kind, and you can still be great friends.
